Appreciate the heads-up — runbook notes below.

Operational constraints we must consider if Nimbus goes 12m reserved:
- Current Dedicated pools have ~220 GPUs nominal capacity in the west-us cluster; 140 GPU block for Nimbus would consume ~64% and reduce headroom for other committed deals in that window.
- Lead time for reallocations: kernel-level tuning and quantization adjustments for Nimbus model family (~2 weeks); provisioning windows typically need 10 business days for physical allocation + canary traffic routing.
- Burst budget: we can cover short spikes up to ~60 GPUs for short intervals but that raises per-token cost by ~18% on average.

Options to present:
A) 12m Reserved with staged tranche — 50 GPUs immediate, +90 GPUs after M1 performance milestone (reduces near-term pressure).
B) 6m Reserved + guaranteed burst credits up to 80 GPUs (cheaper upfront, higher marginal).
C) Dedicated hybrid: reserved for baseline + autoscaling carve-outs scheduled for peak windows (requires SLA exception in contract).

I can model tranche dates and the canary/integration schedule if you confirm which option we want to prioritize for commercial.

Laura Bennett
Head of Dedicated Capacity | Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.com

Subject: Re: Weekly fleet planning: runway tradeoffs tied to pipeline (Nimbus Labs)

Adding infra constraints & risk items:

- Maintenance blackout: west-us cluster has a planned maintenance window 11/20–11/24 for a kernel upgrade — reduces available GPUs by ~12% (affects tranche timing).
- Spare capacity buffer: infra policy recommends a 15% buffer for unexpected hardware OOS/failure during high utilization months (Dec–Feb). If we drop below buffer, we need to trigger burst fallback which is more expensive and introduces queuing latencies.
- Cross-region fallback: we can move part of the burst to east-us but that adds ~30–60ms tail latency depending on KV cache warm-up; acceptable for batch, risky for low-latency apps.

I'll run a resilience scenario assuming A/B/C from Laura and return numbers by EOD Friday. Also tagging a perf note: if Nimbus adopts 8-bit quantized weights we can shave ~25% GPU usage but need model validation.

Marcus Lin
Infrastructure Lead | Redwood Inference
